text:
The computational signals were real. A distinct, transferable new folding mechanism was not established. Reopen only for materially new independent evidence — not another rescue of the existing stack. The audit engine remains a Supported tool. This closeout does not change the Supported four or the UQCF-GEM Git freeze (v15.03).

19 Sep 2026 field note. The author went back through WetLabEngine/UQCF-GEM protein work and tried to falsify the earlier interpretation. The conclusion changed. What looked like a new mechanism was an interesting signal.

Final held-out transfer test of retained structural/coherence history as extra information about future folding, beyond current state, elapsed time, and ordinary trajectory history: one direction +~2.6% (p≈0.46); reverse ~5.6% worse (p≈0.49). Did not transfer. Custom protein-mechanism program CLOSED.

What still stands

Backbone ordering, preorganization, and sequence-dependent effects were measurable (Restricted, in-silico).
Frozen v9 bridge on 1UAO/1L2Y: ordering/RMSD direction, not full folding, not long-range contact closure.
Villin HP35 R_t looked like path-dependent fate; later stronger tests (source recovery, constrained backbones, matched controls, held-out proteins, NO-GO gates) did not establish a new mechanism.
WetLabEngine audit engine (findings.json) remains a Supported tool.

What this corrects

A distinct transferable folding mechanism.
Cross-domain recurrence (quantum, fractal, protein, critical path, TSP) as proof of a common law.
Rewriting the archive after the fact. Positive results, failed hypotheses, methodology problems, recovered source evidence, and the final NO-GO stay public.
